why: train.py line citations still carrying a bare number, in both forms the check reads: the qualified `train.py:NNN` and the abbreviated `:NNN` inside a sentence that names train.py and no sha. A RATCHET -- a NEW bare citation FAILs check_train_cite_targets. Ruling (aupai-4c, 2026-09-06 and the abbreviated-form narrowing 2026-09-07): cite a role or a symbol, or anchor the number to a commit sha. Every entry is DEBT, not an exception: the 2026-09-06 audit read the 198 qualified citations under scripts/ and 103 of 118 judgement cases were rotten, so assume these are mostly rotten too and read each one before believing it. 4c has ordered the audit of these, eval/ first, one commit per directory, shrinking this list each time.
schema: allowed_bare maps `<citing file>-><cited number>` to HOW MANY bare citations that pair may carry. CONTENT-KEYED, NOT POSITION-KEYED, and a MULTISET rather than a set. The first schema keyed on `<file>:<citing line>-><target>` and any insertion above a baselined citation moved its key, turning the ratchet red on whoever merged next (4c, 2026-09-07; e1 hit it landing #48, 122 lines inserted, key 6174 -> 6285). A line-text hash was the other candidate and trades one false red for another: measured, it gives 87 distinct keys for 87 citations against this key's 70, but it goes red on a comment REFLOW, which happens whenever a sentence around a citation is edited. The count is what keeps the ratchet honest under a colliding key: 15 pairs carry more than one citation, so a set would let a file grow from one to three with the baseline unchanged.
count_growth_reason: 2, from 125 at facts/ entry. THE SWEEP IS CLOSED: both remaining citations are quoted tool output and neither can become a symbol without falsifying a quotation. eff.recompile_reason_named holds TORCH_LOGS=recompiles' own lines, 'Recompiling function forward in /work/aupai/train.py:521' and the muon_update one at :746 -- the tool printed those at the tree the run used, they are not pointers this repo maintains, and the entry says so in its own text. Everything else resolved: 74 of 74 citations judged across the six facts/ files were rotten, code side zero since 2026-09-07 morning, 19 sha-anchored and verified at their sha. THE THREE CLASSES, because they are not interchangeable and a future sweep will meet them again: (1) the ordinary case, 14 entries that already named the symbol beside the number, where the number was redundant and dropping it lost nothing; (2) quoted tool output, kept verbatim, the two above; (3) a citation describing a defect that has SINCE BEEN FIXED -- eff.run_end_cursor_overstates_under_max_steps, whose five numbers describe the run-end save before c9011022 gave it opt and step. A symbol there would aim a reader at code that now does the opposite, and a confidently wrong symbol is worse than a visibly stale number; a content search over every train.py commit 2026-08-28..2026-09-05 found no sha holding all five at their lines (best 2 of 5), so it carries 'lines as recorded' and names the fixing commit. Two more were JSON KEYS rather than prose (eff.layer9_mixer_o_lags' default_off_read_not_inferred maps a citation to the symbol found there) and took a sha anchor from the entry's own the_one_commit, 169da865, where both lines are verbatim -- the claim is about the tree that INTRODUCED the flag, so the pointer has to resolve against that tree. A new bare citation anywhere FAILs.
